docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This datasheet has been created to document my contributions to the Trash Canner project. In this datasheet I will show my block diagram, component selection, bill of materials, schematic design, and power budget.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text: The Trash Canner project is showcase our team's process on designing an automatic trashcan that uses a force and distance sensor. The force sensor will read the total weight of the trash in the can and use a LED scale to show how close the contents of the can are to the recommended weight capacity to prevent the bag from ripping. The distance sensor will detect the can's rough fullness and alert the user to take out the trash via sound cue when it reaches the suggested maximum capacity. A link to the team report can be found here.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text: My contribution to this project is the distance sensor subsystem. The distance sensor will activate once the lid of the trashcan is closed. Once activated, the sensor will start reading values based on how close the trash is to the lid. After the trash gets too close to the sensor, the sensor will send a signal to cue a sound to play that alerts the user to change trashbag because it is at maximum capacity.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This diagram shows the circuit that involves a force sensor, voltage regulator, op-amp, speaker, LED, and a PIC nano provided by the class. These parts have been selected because they have already been tested in class, meaning I have some prior experience with them. As for the type of sensor, I decided on an IR sensor because it is useful when measuring shorter distances. The circuit will be supplied with a 5V power supply and will also be connected both the circuit with the force sensor as they will need to work in conjunction to meet our standards for the trash can's alert system. Once the value for the IR sensor has reached a certain threshold, the PIC will send a signal for the speaker to alert the user that the trash is at capacity and needs to be thrown out.

Choice: Option 2: CTX936TR-ND surface mount oscillator

Rationale: A clock oscillator is easier to work with because it requires no external circuitry in order to interface with the PSoC. This is particularly important because we are not sure of the electrical characteristics of the PCB, which could affect the oscillation of a crystal. While the shipping speed is slow, according to the website if we order this week it will arrive within 3 weeks.
